sections.heading: What Is an Insulated Glass Unit and Why Does It Fail?
sections.body: An insulated glass unit, commonly called an IGU, consists of two or more panes of glass separated by a spacer and sealed to create an insulating air or gas-filled chamber. This design reduces heat transfer and helps maintain interior comfort year-round. Over time, however, the perimeter seal that holds everything together can degrade. Once the seal fails, outside air and moisture infiltrate the chamber, causing the familiar cloudy or foggy appearance between the panes. In Arlington's climate, where temperatures swing significantly between humid summers and cold winters, thermal stress accelerates seal wear. UV exposure, building movement, and age all contribute as well. A failed IGU does not self-correct — the fogging only worsens, and the insulating performance of the unit drops substantially. Identifying seal failure early and scheduling professional replacement is the best way to restore your window's function before the problem spreads to adjacent units or causes secondary issues like water intrusion along the frame.

sections.heading: Residential IGU Replacement in Arlington Neighborhoods
sections.body: Homeowners across Arlington neighborhoods — from the tree-lined streets of Lyon Village to the newer construction in the Shirlington area — frequently encounter IGU failure in double-pane windows and sliding glass doors. The most visible sign is persistent fogging or condensation trapped between the panes that cannot be wiped away. Other indicators include visible moisture streaks, white mineral deposits left by evaporated water, and a noticeable reduction in the comfort of rooms adjacent to affected windows. Rather than replacing entire window frames, most homeowners can save significant time and money by replacing only the failed glass unit itself. Our technicians measure the existing unit precisely, order a matching replacement, and install it cleanly within the original frame. This approach preserves your home's appearance and eliminates the mess and extended timelines associated with full window replacement projects.

sections.heading: The IGU Replacement Process: What to Expect
sections.body: Our replacement process begins with an on-site assessment at your Arlington property. A technician evaluates the affected units, confirms that the frames are structurally sound and suitable for IGU-only replacement, and takes precise measurements. We then source replacement units built to match your existing glass specifications, including thickness, low-e coatings if present, and overall dimensions. Lead times vary based on unit size and glass specifications, and we communicate realistic timelines upfront so you can plan accordingly. On installation day, the technician carefully removes the failed unit, cleans and inspects the frame pocket, sets the new IGU with appropriate glazing tape or compound, and secures it properly within the frame system. Most single-unit residential replacements are completed in a few hours. Commercial projects involving multiple units are sequenced to keep disruption manageable. Before leaving, we inspect the finished installation and confirm the new unit is properly sealed and seated.

faq.q: How do I know if my insulated glass unit needs replacement?
faq.a: The most common sign is persistent fogging or condensation between the panes that you cannot wipe away. You may also notice white or cloudy streaks, a slight distortion in the glass, or rooms that feel drafty near windows that previously felt comfortable. If you observe any of these signs, a professional assessment can confirm whether IGU replacement is the right solution.

faq.q: Can the IGU be replaced without replacing the entire window frame?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. If the window frame itself is structurally sound, only the glass unit needs to be replaced. This is typically faster, less disruptive, and more affordable than a full window replacement. Our technicians assess the frame condition during the initial visit to confirm that IGU-only replacement is appropriate for your specific situation.

faq.q: How long does insulated glass unit replacement take?
faq.a: A single residential IGU replacement is typically completed in a few hours on the day of installation. The larger time factor is usually the lead time for the replacement unit to be manufactured and delivered, which varies based on the size and specifications of the glass. We provide realistic timelines during the assessment so you can plan accordingly.
